(1) 0207A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'Unde : Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus nisi super humilem et quietum? etc. (Isa. LXVI).' Migne's reading shares almost nothing with the Clementine's Is 66:2, and the gloss that follows rests on his 'quietum'. (2) 0207A WITHDRAWAL, and it would have been a false [sic:]: our twin reads 'et tanta calliditate circum venit', a split run that satisfies Pattern 10 exactly. The plate breaks circum | venit ACROSS A LINE END WITH NO HYPHEN -- one word, circumvenit. Same class as 8957's Per eat / Pereat. Marker withdrawn. (3) 0208B CONFIRMED: Migne really does invert the word order, 'et clamitet : Digitus Dei hic est :', against 'Digitus Dei est hic' printed five other times in this stint's range and in Ex 8:19. Both are sound Latin, English has no exponent for the order, so no marker fires; crux only. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'Memento diem sabbati sanctificare' (the second [var:] site); 'Vacate et videte quoniam ego sum Deus'; 'Sicut Jamnes et Mambres ... homines mente corrupti, reprobi circa fidem, etc. (II Tim. III)' -- Jamnes and the inverted mente corrupti are both Migne's; 'quamvis de Filio non tacuerunt'; 'Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam'; the bracketed variant '[Al., Cynicorum]' in roman brackets; and every negation of the Augustine quaestio at 0208C ('non conati sunt', 'non autem fuerant', 'nec potuerunt', 'nihil de illius terrae separatione', 'nec auderent conari').

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers. THREE FINDINGS. (1) 0209B, a TRANSCRIPTION divergence: the plate sets the attribution as an ordinary roman parenthetical, 'VERS. 32. -- Et ingravatum est, etc. (AUG., quaest. 29.)', with only quaest. in italic, exactly like every other siglum on the page. Our twin wraps the WHOLE parenthetical in italics and marks it as no note at all. Filed as a pending TEI patch; the English keeps the twin's structure so that note parity holds, and the patch will convert both sides together. (2) 0209D WITHDRAWAL, and it would have been a false claim in either direction: our twin reads 'Non maechaberis'; THE PLATE PRINTS THE OE LIGATURE, 'Non moechaberis'. So Migne agrees with Ex 20:14 exactly and there is no Vulgate divergence at all. Confirmed against an internal control -- the same book prints 'quaedam moechia' at 0215D, where our twin has oe correctly. Filed as a pending TEI patch. (3) 0210D CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'Addit etiam his : O homo, tu qui es qui respondeas Deo (Rom. IX).' Migne prints a relative where Rom 9:20 has the interrogative 'tu quis es'. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: '(RAB. in Exod., tom. II.)'; '(AUG., quaest. 30.)'; 'Ingravavit Pharao cor suum etiam in hoc tempore, et noluit dimittere populum' and 'Certe nunc non dictum est ... sed ingravavit Pharao cor suum'; 'usque ad Vacate et videte, quoniam ego sum Deus'; '(GREG., lib. XVIII Moral., c. 28, tom. II.)'; 'Ergo cui vult miseretur' (Migne's cui for Rom 9:18's cujus; declined); 'nec Aaron nec Moyses aliquid manu operantur', 'spargere non in terram sed in coelum' and 'Neque enim nihil' at 0210A-B, all negations intact; 'non dicitur, Induratum est cor Pharaonis' and 'induratur quidem cor Pharaonis, sed non a Domino' at 0210B-C.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns in the bands opened. TWO FINDINGS. (1) 0211A CONFIRMED, and it is the control for the 0210D [var:]: eleven lines below the broken reading, Migne sets the SAME VERSE CORRECTLY -- 'deterret dicens Rom. IX : O homo, quis es qui respondeas Deo.' Two columns, two crops, two distinct readings of Rom 9:20 by the same compositor. Note the terminal FULL STOP, not a question mark; Pattern 8 keeps it. (2) 0211A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: '(RAB.) Septimum praeceptum : Non furaberis;' -- Migne's wording is Rom 13:9's, not Ex 20:15's 'Non furtum facies'. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: the bracketed variant 'curiosius [curiosus]' in roman brackets; 'Et audivit arcana verba, quae non licet homini loqui'; '(AUG., quaest. 35 in Exod., tom. III.)'; 'ne jumenta interirent omnia'; 'Mosem non juberi omnia miranda facere virga'; the bracketed variant 'Mosi [Moses]' at 0212B; 'nec dicitur quod intraverint Moses et Aaron ad eum ... et non poterant resistere Mosi'; 'nec intrat, sed vocatur ad Pharaonem'. AND 0212C CONFIRMED, declined: 'de quo dicit Dominus Luc. xii : Ignem veni mittere in terra (Luc. xii).' Migne prints the ablative 'in terra' for Lc 12:49's accusative 'in terram', AND prints the Luke reference twice, once in the running text and once as a parenthetical. Both are his; the doubling is his ordinary citing habit and is not dittography, and the single-letter case variant is below the Pattern 14 bar. No marker on either.

(1) 0217A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: 'propheta dicit : Butyrum et mel manducabit ; priusquam faciat aut proferat maligna, eliget bonum (Isa. VII); quoniam priusquam sciat puer bonum aut malum, resistet malitiae, ut eligat quod bonum est.' Is 7:15 reads 'Butyrum et mel comedet, ut sciat reprobare malum, et eligere bonum' -- a wholly different second clause -- and Origen's continuation picks up Migne's priusquam. (2) 0217B CONFIRMED, the stint's only [sic:]: 'qui permanet in iniquitate, tanquam plumbum demergitur in profondum.' The plate really prints profondum with an o, and EIGHT LINES ABOVE, on the same plate and in the same sentence-chain, it prints 'ut exeat de profundo' with a u. Corpus control run before firing: profondum occurs ONCE in the whole chunked Latin corpus, against profund- five times in this book alone including the instance in its own paragraph. Non-word, Migne's, internal control on the same plate. [sic: *profondum*] with the sense rendered beside it per the 2026-09-05 amendment. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'Delicta juventutis meae et ignorantias meas ne memineris (Psal. XXIV)'; 'nisi post haec omnia in infidelitate perdurans, nolit jungi Israeliticae plebi'; '(AUG. in libro Locutionum.)'; 'Non audiet vos Pharao'; and at 0217D 'qui apud Hebraeos Nisam, apud Macedones Xanthikos dicitur' with Greek type, against 'Hic est Nisan, secundum Hebraeos' printed eight lines below -- both Migne's, DECLINED as a proper-name variant on the 8950 Bethehem/Bethlehem precedent.

(2) 0219B UNRESOLVED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT SO: our twin prints the Greek 'aionion' fully formed with an iota; the plate, at 6x native, prints what reads as alpha, a VISIBLE GAP, then omega with smooth breathing and grave, and NO IOTA. The word is certainly the one Augustine's quaestio is about, but whether the iota is absent from Migne's setting, worn, or lost in this photograph cannot be told from one witness, and the archive copy is 1-bit JBIG2 and may never be sole witness for a letter. No marker, no patch; filed in the pending-patches file as needing a second witness, and the English carries the twin's reading verbatim. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 0219A 'Phase. Hebraice est Pesach [Hebrew], Graece Pascha, id est, transitus' -- the recovered Hebrew is on the plate exactly where the brief says, carried into the English verbatim and NOT re-opened; 0219B 'VERS. 14-17. -- Habebitis autem hanc diem' with the feminine hanc against Ex 12:14's hunc, and Augustine's own 'Et facietis diem hunc' masculine three lines below (Pattern 9: no English exponent, crux only); the bracketed variant 'azyma jubemur [jubentur] comedere' at 0219C; 0219C 'Quicunque baptizati sumus in Christo Jesu, in mortem ipsius baptizati sumus, etc. (Gal. ONE FINDING, no marker. 0221A CONFIRMED: 'Si vis perfectus esse, vade et vende omnia quae habes, et da pauperibus, et habebis thesaurum in coelo, et veni, sequere me (Matth. VI), hoc est proficisci de Ramesse, et sequi Christum.' The quotation is Matthew 19:21 and Migne's locator says Matthew VI. The cause is visible two lines above on the same plate: the gloss has just alluded to Mt 6:19-20, 'ne thesaurizes ubi tinea exterminat, et fures effodiunt', and the locator has migrated onto the following quotation. Migne's citation, so it rides verbatim and takes no marker; recorded in the cruces. The quotation also reads 'vade et vende OMNIA quae habes' where Mt 19:21 has 'vade, vende quae habes' -- Luke 18:22's omnia, a conflation, declined. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: 'quae interpretatur commotio tineae'; 'vasa aurea et argentea ; cum vestibus, id est, corporibus'.
